record.title: NostrAgent combines decentralized agent identity, scoped delegation, trust attestations and Lightning payment
record.summary: The paper proposes NostrAgent, which places agent identity declarations, narrowing delegation chains and peer attestations in signed Nostr events, with Lightning HTTP 402 payment bound to agent identity. Its Python prototype reports depth-4 delegation verification at 0.0619 ms median (900 measurements) and a full L402 flow at 157.4 ms median (90 runs) on a local Docker regtest setup. The authors say 17 of 19 failure modes passed empirical tests, one was bounded analytically and one remains an architectural limitation. These are author-reported prototype results: experiments used a fixed seed on Apple Silicon/macOS with Python 3.11, and the linked replication package was not run independently. The paper also reports trust-query latency rising to 2.42 seconds at 500 synthetic nodes and identifies public attestation metadata and relay-consistency limits.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper proposes three signed Nostr event kinds for agent identity, narrowing delegation chains and peer attestations, and binds Lightning HTTP 402 payments to an agent identity; it describes operator-controlled identity and offline authorization replay.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the authors’ fixed-seed prototype evaluation, depth-4 delegation verification had a 0.0619 ms median over 900 measurements, and the full Lightning-settled L402 flow had a 157.4 ms median over 90 runs on a local Docker regtest testbed. The authors report 17/19 failure modes passed empirical tests; one was bounded analytically and one disclosed as a limitation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper links a replication package with implementation, benchmark harness, raw results, Docker testbed and tests. The evaluation is fixed-seed on Apple Silicon/macOS with Python 3.11; the paper reports a 2.422 s median trust query at 500 synthetic nodes and identifies relay consistency and public attestation metadata as trade-offs. This activation did not run the artifact.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent execution of the linked replication package was performed, and no external implementation or deployment was inspected.

The paper does not establish interoperability with deployed agent frameworks or standardized Nostr event kinds, and the comparison against centralized/more expressive systems is architectural rather than head-to-head operational.
The largest reported trust graph is synthetic and query latency rises sharply at 500 nodes; real deployment graph shape and privacy acceptability are unmeasured.

brief.importance_rationale: If the architecture's local prototype results generalize, combining operator-controlled identity, verifiable scope attenuation, revocation, peer attestations and payment-bound identity could inform concrete agent-delegation system designs. Score 4 reflects a meaningful but specialized infrastructure contribution; the evidence is one paper's prototype, not production deployment or independent reproduction.
limitations: All measured results are from one author-run prototype and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The evaluation uses fixed seed 42, one Apple Silicon/macOS host and Python 3.11; Docker flows use a private regtest network, not Bitcoin mainnet or production relays.
Trust-query median latency reaches 2.422 seconds on 500-node synthetic graphs under the reported settings.
The attestation graph is public and exposes relationship metadata; this privacy cost is a design trade-off, not a measured deployment outcome.
The paper identifies relay-only consistency/divergence limits, a pre-rotation propagation window and a single-level key-rotation equivocation gap.
The authors report 17 of 19 failure modes pass empirically; one is bounded analytically and one remains an architectural limitation.
brief.summary: The paper proposes NostrAgent, which places agent identity declarations, narrowing delegation chains and peer attestations in signed Nostr events, with Lightning HTTP 402 payment bound to agent identity. Its Python prototype reports depth-4 delegation verification at 0.0619 ms median (900 measurements) and a full L402 flow at 157.4 ms median (90 runs) on a local Docker regtest setup. The authors say 17 of 19 failure modes passed empirical tests, one was bounded analytically and one remains an architectural limitation. These are author-reported prototype results: experiments used a fixed seed on Apple Silicon/macOS with Python 3.11, and the linked replication package was not run independently. The paper also reports trust-query latency rising to 2.42 seconds at 500 synthetic nodes and identifies public attestation metadata and relay-consistency limits.

technical.claimed_result: Author-run prototype reports 0.0619 ms median for depth-4 offline delegation verification, 157.4 ms median for full L402 settlement on regtest, 17/19 empirically passing failure modes, and linear chain-depth scaling.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper measures local verification and a regtest payment flow; it does not provide production-scale hardware/cost accounting or mainnet settlement results.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected paper provides detailed architecture, fixed-seed benchmark tables and a linked replication package. Performance and security outcomes remain paper-reported and were not independently reproduced here.
technical.implementation_status: Research prototype with author-linked replication package; production deployment and Nostr kind standardization are not established.
technical.mechanism: Kind 38100 identity events use BIP340 signatures and pre-rotation commitments; Kind 38101 delegation chains require each hop to narrow capabilities; Kind 38102 peer attestations form a trust graph. Lightning HTTP 402 payment is bound to agent identity, while Nostr relays act as substitutable transport rather than a trust root.
technical.regime: Python prototype; Apple Silicon/macOS host, Python 3.11, fixed seed 42. Offline benchmarks use 900 measurements after 100 warm-ups. Docker testbed uses three strfry relays, two LND nodes and one bitcoind node in private regtest; stateful flows use 90 runs after warm-up.
technical.reproducibility: Paper reports fixed seed, environment, run counts and benchmark methods and links implementation, harness, raw results, Docker testbed and tests. The artifact was not run independently in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: The reported evaluation compares configurations and failure modes within the prototype; it does not establish a head-to-head production comparison with centralized identity, OAuth/DID composition or more expressive capability systems.

brief.title: NostrAgent combines decentralized agent identity, scoped delegation, trust attestations and Lightning payment
brief.why_it_matters: Cross-agent delegation needs identity continuity, least-authority scopes, revocation, trust and payment across organizational boundaries. NostrAgent offers one concrete composition and measures some local verification costs, which can inform architecture choices for decentralized agent services. Its constrained setup and disclosed scaling, privacy and consistency costs mean it does not establish production readiness or that the design is preferable to centralized or more expressive alternatives.
